questions.def: Third conditional: If + past perfect, would have + past participle.
questions.question: If I had known, I ___ you.

questions.def: First conditional: If + present simple, will + base form.
questions.question: If it ___, we'll stay home.

questions.def: Use 'known' after 'had' in a third conditional: Had I known...
questions.question: Had I knew about the delay, I'd have rescheduled.

questions.def: Third conditional: 'had eaten' is past perfect tense.
questions.question: If I ___ all that cake, I'd feel sick.

questions.def: Unless = if not. First conditional: will + base form.
questions.question: Unless it rains, we ___ to the park.

questions.def: Second conditional: if + past simple, would + base form.
questions.question: She ___ the job if she spoke English.

questions.def: Use 'were' instead of 'was' in second conditional advice.
questions.question: If I was you, I will tell him.

questions.def: Second conditional: 'were' after 'if' for hypothetical situations.
questions.question: If I ___ taller, I could play basketball.

questions.def: Third conditional: If + past perfect, would have + past participle.
questions.question: If you ___ harder, you would have passed.

questions.def: Third conditional: would have + past participle.
questions.question: I ___ you if I had known.

questions.def: Incorrect use of 'would' in the 'if' clause. Use 'had studied'.
questions.question: If she would studied, she would pass the test.

questions.def: First conditional: present simple in the 'if' clause.
questions.question: If it ___ well, we will celebrate.

questions.def: Second conditional: If + past simple, would + base form.
questions.question: If I ___ enough money, I would travel.

questions.def: Second conditional: 'were' is used for hypothetical situations.
questions.question: If I ___ you, I would call her.

questions.def: Incorrect use of 'will' in the 'if' clause. Use 'listen'.
questions.question: If you will listen, I will tell you.

questions.def: Second conditional: past simple in the 'if' clause.
questions.question: If I ___ the answer, I would tell you.

questions.def: Third conditional: would have + past participle.
questions.question: If she had arrived earlier, she ___ him.

questions.def: Unless = if not. First conditional: present simple.
questions.question: Unless you ___, you'll miss the bus.

questions.def: No 'would' after 'if'. It should be 'If I go...'
questions.question: If I would go, I will take you.

questions.def: First conditional: present simple in the 'if' clause.
questions.question: If it ___ tomorrow, we'll stay inside.

questions.def: Second conditional: if + past simple, would + base form.
questions.question: If he ___ harder, he would pass the test.

questions.def: Third conditional: would have + past participle.
questions.question: If I hadn't been late, I ___ the meeting.

questions.def: Correct conditional is: If she has time, she will help you.
questions.question: If she has time, she will help you.

questions.def: Second conditional: 'were' is the correct form after 'if'.
questions.question: If I ___ you, I wouldn't do that.

questions.def: Third conditional: 'would have' + past participle.
questions.question: If they had listened, they ___ the mistake.

questions.def: First conditional: 'will' in the main clause.
questions.question: What ___ if you lose your job?

questions.def: Second conditional: past simple after 'if'.
questions.question: If I ___ her number, I would call.

questions.def: Zero conditional: present simple for general truths.
questions.question: If you mix red and blue, you ___ purple.

questions.def: Third conditional: would have + past participle.
questions.question: I ___ you, if I had known you needed help.

questions.def: Third conditional: If + past perfect, would have + past participle.
questions.question: If I had known, I ___ you.
